## #25968 reverted: what the wall placement did to the whole-package shards, and why the model missed it

#25968 (wall-model bin placement + the 2026-10-26 refresh + CLI ×4) landed at 08:35Z. It is being reverted by #26077 (card #26074), because merge_group Test Core went red on 5 of 27 full builds since 08:16Z, against 0 of 19 on the old layout. Every red was a load-sensitive test: objectql hook-run-as on cold import, plugin-security shipped-sets taking more than 5s, and the cli hook-timeout CONTROL test. This comment records the mechanism so that a second attempt can avoid it. No acceptance reading was taken, because the layout is being reverted.

### Placement, full list (`turbo ls`, dogfood excluded), replayed through `planRun()`

Each cell is the whole-package seconds on that shard, with the package count in brackets.

| shard | before: main cdd4eea9 (plain sum, 10-23 dataset, cli ×3) | after: #25968 (wall placement, 10-26 refresh, cli ×4) |
|---|---|---|
| 1/8 | 1866 (6) | 186 (6) + cli 1/4 674 |
| 2/8 | 1866 (11) **objectql** | 185 (6) + cli 2/4 674 |
| 3/8 | 900 (8) + cli 1/3 966 | 185 (6) + cli 3/4 674 |
| 4/8 | 900 (9) + cli 2/3 966 | 185 (6) + cli 4/4 674 |
| 5/8 | 899 (8) + cli 3/3 966 **plugin-security** | 2141 (12) |
| 6/8 | 1866 (10) | 2139 (20) |
| 7/8 | 1868 (11) | 2141 (13) **objectql + plugin-security** |
| 8/8 | 1866 (19) | 2142 (13) |

Clearing the whole-package leg off the slice shards moved about 2,850 s of four-wide work onto the other shards. Before, five shards each carried about 1,866 s. After, four shards each carried about 2,141 s, which is 15% more contended time per shard. objectql and plugin-security ended up on the same shard. Before the change, plugin-security had sat on a slice shard with only 899 s of whole-package work.

The cli test `test/hook-timeout-override-refusal.test.ts` moved from slice 1/3 to slice 2/4. vitest's sha1 split was reproduced locally and matches run 40274911131 file for file. A slice runs alone after its shard's whole leg, so that test's neighbours are cli files only.

### Why the wall model missed it

- `wholeSum / 2.9 + slice` predicts a shard's step time, which is a throughput figure. It says nothing about how slow one test runs while other suites share the leg. Each shard's step did fall to ~738 s in the prediction, but the tests that broke have per-test wall budgets, and those budgets depend on what runs alongside them.
- The density cap (2697 s) is a ceiling on plain sums. 2141 s passed it, so nothing in the self-test graded co-run intensity or which suites share a leg.
- This partitioner has seen this failure before. Its `FILE_SHARDED_PACKAGES` history records that #22415 placed slices at 4× weight, piled the remaining whole packages onto three shards at ~2641 s, and inflated windows 1.5–1.9× until it was reverted (806b03e2ae). #25968 used 2.9× and reached 2141 s. That is milder, but it is the same mechanism, and the queue's load-sensitive tests are what detected it.

### For a second attempt

- Read any placement change against the merge-queue red rate as well as shard wall.
- **Lowest-risk candidate, replayed:** the old plain-sum placement with the 10-26 refresh and cli ×4. The 2026-11-02 refresh will hit pin 3c at ×3 again, so cli ×4 is needed anyway. In the replay, whole-package shards come out at ~1500 s each, which is less than today's 1866 s. Slice shards come out at 826 s whole + 674 s slice, giving a predicted step of 959 s against 1277 s today. objectql and plugin-security land on different shards (7/8 and 6/8). This needs no change to placement logic.
- If whole-package work is moved off the slice shards again, cap each shard's whole sum at roughly the old mean, or keep the known load-sensitive suites apart (objectql, plugin-security), or weight the whole leg by a measured co-run slowdown rather than a flat 2.9.
- Option B, declarations only on the slice that reads `.d.ts` (Tier H, ci.yml), shortens the slice shards without moving any package.

## After-landing reading for #26186: 10 full Test Core queue builds, 0 red

#26186 merged at 2026-10-26 18:02Z. I read it at 00:45Z over REST: every `merge_group` run of `ci.yml` created from 17:43Z on, which is the run for #26186's own group and everything queued on top of it.

**All queue builds:** 96 completed runs, 96 green. No job in any of them failed, no run was re-attempted, and no entry was ejected by Test Core. Two more were still in progress at read time.

### The first 10 full builds

A build counts as full here when two things hold. First, at least 6 of its 8 Test Core shards ran 10 minutes or more. Second, the aggregator's suite list shows objectql, plugin-security and all 4 cli slices executed. The ratios below are each suite's measured wall against its suite-duration ceiling, from the aggregator's report-only check.

(#26264 was built twice because its first group was rebuilt after an entry ahead of it changed. Both builds were green.)

- **Test Core: 10 of 10 green, and 96 of 96 over all queue builds since landing.** For comparison, the #25968 layout went red 5 times in 27. None of the three load-sensitive tests timed out: objectql `hook-run-as`, plugin-security `shipped-sets-identity-default-row-scope`, and cli `hook-timeout-override-refusal`.
- **The suites that read over their ceilings under #25968 now read under them.** On that layout, plugin-security measured 605–611 s against its 474 s ceiling (1.28x), objectql 1.16x, plugin-auth up to 1.55x and driver-sql 1.34–1.36x (#26077 body). On these 10 builds the four read 0.37–0.88x. Across all 29 heavy builds since landing, plugin-security reached its ceiling once, at 1.00x. objectql, plugin-auth and driver-sql never did.
- **One standing over-ceiling reading, which is report-only:** `@objectstack/service-package` reads 33–77 s against a 32.90 s ceiling (1.1–2.3x) on 26 of the 29 heavy builds. It was already over on the old layout before this PR: 47.89 s on 40325660507 and 46.97 s on 40327508710 (about 1.45x). Its suite gained a hydration test file in #26054 at 10:42Z, and its ceiling is the 10-26 refresh's figure. The check reports and does not fail. I'm noting it here and not filing it.

### Slowest spec-touching `pull_request` shard (for information, not the gate)

There have been 9 spec-touching PRs since landing (#26138 #26159 #26271 #26305 #26320 #26342 #26343 #26355 #26361). Their completed Test Core runs:

| run | PR | slowest shard |
|---|---|--:|
| 40375258805 | #26271 | 29.2 min (5/8) |
| 40391655385 | #26305 | 24.6 min (5/8) |
| 40399971776 | #26320 | 24.8 min (5/8) |

| 40420137578 | #26361 | 24.6 min (5/8) |
| 40423632426 | #26343 | 25.1 min (5/8) |

The slowest spec-PR shard is 23.9–25.4 min on 8 of these 10 runs. The outliers are 20.7 and 29.2. Before #25968 the range was 25.7–28.8, so this is about 2–4 min faster. It does not reach the original ≤ ~20 min goal. The slowest shard is always a CLI-slice shard: setup, then the cold DTS closure (~6 min), then ~5 min of whole packages, then a slice. The step model's prediction of 959 s plus the closure and setup gives about 23.5 min, which is what these runs read. #26138's earlier run 40377181895 was red on cli slices 4/8 and 6/8. That red was a real assertion in that PR's own CLI change (`audit-mail-bodies.archive.integration.test.ts` › "a declared archive this boot cannot connect is NOT reported clean", 1 ms, not a timeout), and the PR's next run was green.

**For the seat:** the acceptance gate (no load-shaped red in the queue) holds. The speed goal is still open. What is left on a slice shard is the DTS closure plus the slice, which brings option B (DTS only on the slice that reads `.d.ts`, Tier H, ci.yml) or option C (weight-balanced CLI slices) from the earlier report back on the table. Choosing between them is the seat's or the maintainer's call. I have not taken either.
